injuryReports.name: Chad Ryland
injuryReports.returnComment: Ryland played just three snaps during the loss, though he managed to convert his only kick, which came from 28 yards and also served as the team's only points in the game. Ryland has now converted 20 of his 22 field-goal attempts and 16 of his 17 extra-point tries across nine games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Ryland made his lone field-goal attempt during Arizona's loss versus the Seahawks on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Hjalte Froholdt
injuryReports.returnComment: Froholdt played all 51 of the Cardinals' offensive snaps during Sunday's game at Seattle, but he may have suffered a concussion somewhere along the way. He'll need to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol, which includes getting clearance from an independent neurologist, before he'll be able to return to game action. With Jon Gaines nursing an ankle injury, Arizona could be forced to turn to 2025 sixth-rounder Hayden Conner, who has limited experience, for reps at center.
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Carson Beck
injuryReports.returnComment: Beck is slated to take over as Arizona's starting quarterback in Week 10, with Gardner Minshew (elbow) potentially set to miss the remainder of the 2026 season with a torn UCL. Beck has yet to appear in a regular-season contest in his rookie campaign, but he completed 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown in his lone preseason appearance. Lead running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is still on injured reserve for at least three more contests and top wide receiver Michael Wilson (neck) suffered a season-ending injury in Week 9, so Beck will have to make do with limited options around him in Arizona.
injuryReports.injury: Beck is expected to start Sunday's contest against the Rams, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Gardner Minshew II
injuryReports.returnComment: Minshew's stint as the Cardinals' starting QB thus is shaping up to be a brief one. Assuming Schefter's report is confirmed, Carson Beck is slated to take over as Arizona's QB1, beginning with this Sunday's game against the Rams.
injuryReports.injury: Elbow

injuryReports.name: Michael Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: With the Cardinals' top WR now sidelined and presumably headed to season-ending IR, Reggie Virgil, Simi Fehoko, Harrison Wallace and Devin Duvernay currently are the wide receivers on the team's active roster. Additionally, Shedrick Jackson, Zay Jones and James Proche are on Arizona's practice squad, but look for further reinforcements to be considered by the Cardinals in the coming days.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Jayden Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Bam Knight
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Jon Gaines II
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Tyler Allgeier
injuryReports.returnComment: Allegeier has reeled off 10-plus touches in four straight contests, a span in which he's turned 65 touches into 334 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs. He's been the beneficiary of repeated ankle injuries to rookie first-round pick Jeremiyah Love, who must remain on IR for at least three more outings after Sunday's matchup, and the other current top RB on the active roster (Bam Knight) is in the concussion protocol, which will require clearance from an independent neurologist for his next game action. As a result, Allgeier is set up to retain a significant workload until Knight gets the all clear to return.
injuryReports.injury: Allgeier compiled 17 carries for 46 yards and caught two of three targets for no yards during Sunday's 17-3 defeat at Seattle.

injuryReports.name: Trey McBride
injuryReports.returnComment: With QB Jacoby Brissett getting traded to Baltimore this past week, McBride was on the receiving end of passes from Gardner Minshew, and the result was the tight end's fourth-fewest receiving yards in a game this season and also the fourth time he didn't reach the end zone through nine contests. On a positive note, McBride extended his streak with at least seven receptions to 11 outings, which matches the second-longest streak in NFL history, trailing only the 14 Antonio Brown put together from 2014-2015. McBride may have a tough task on his hands next Sunday against the Rams' surging defense.
injuryReports.injury: McBride recorded seven catches (on eight targets) for 54 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss at Seattle.

injuryReports.name: Roy Lopez
injuryReports.returnComment: Lopez sustained a toe injury late in the first half, and he will now be forced to miss the rest of Week 9. In his absence, Andrew Billings is a top candidate to continue to see added snaps at defensive tackle against Seattle.
injuryReports.injury: Toe

injuryReports.name: Max Melton
injuryReports.returnComment: Melton logged consecutive limited practices to end Week 9 prep. The cornerback appears to have overcome his knee injury in time to play in Sunday's contest, leaving Kalen King to remain in a reserve role for Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Melton (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Walter Nolen III
injuryReports.returnComment: Nolen's trio of limited practices during Week 9 prep proves enough to allow the defensive tackle to suit up for Sunday's game. The 23-year-old accumulated 14 tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, in the 2026 regular season before missing consecutive contests with an ankle injury.
injuryReports.injury: Nolen (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Isaiah Adams
injuryReports.returnComment: Adams was placed on IR in early October and missed the required four games. He was designated to return Wednesday and was limited in all three of Arizona's practices this week. Now that he's been activated, Adams is eligible to suit up Sunday, and if he returns he'll likely reclaim his starting role at right guard.
injuryReports.injury: The Cardinals activated Adams (ankle) off injured reserve Saturday, and he remains questionable for Sunday's matchup against the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Elijah Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: Wideout Michael Wilson missed a portion of the contest due to an injury to his ribs, and Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) exited for good late in the first half. That resulted in a need for other Cardinals pass catchers to step up, and Higgins ended up getting targeted a season-high four times. However, he didn't do much with the opportunity, finishing with his lowest yardage total since he was shut out in Week 2. Meanwhile, No. 1 tight end Trey McBride had another big game with seven catches for 72 yards and a touchdown on eight targets. McBride's elite status will likely continue to make Higgins an afterthought most weeks.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins tallied two catches for 10 yards on four targets Sunday in a 33-30 overtime win over Dallas.

injuryReports.name: Reggie Virgil
injuryReports.returnComment: Virgil played a season-high 38 offensive snaps, but he went without a reception for the third straight week. The Cardinals placed Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) on injured reserve Tuesday after the wide receiver fractured his right tibia in Week 8, so more opportunities could come Virgil's way moving forward. Regardless of an increase in workload, the team's Week 9 matchup versus Seattle will be a challenging one for the 22-year-old.
injuryReports.injury: Virgil failed to reel in either of his targets during Sunday's 33-30 overtime victory against Dallas.

injuryReports.name: Devin Duvernay
injuryReports.returnComment: Duvernay reeled in his first two passes of the year while playing 34 offensive snaps in the victory. Fellow wideout Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) fractured his right tibia during the contest, and he is likely set to miss the rest of the 2026 campaign. Duvernay will likely see an increased role on offense in Bourne's absence, but he will remain an unappealing fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup against Seattle.
injuryReports.injury: Duvernay caught both of his targets for 14 yards while also adding 75 yards as a kick returner and 12 punt-return yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime win against the Cowboys.

injuryReports.name: Simi Fehoko
injuryReports.returnComment: Buried on the depth chart at receiver to begin the season, Fehoko mostly served as a special-teams contributor through the Cardinals' first seven games. However,the Cardinals have since traded away Marvin Harrison before losing Jalen Brooks (wrist) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) to season-ending injuries within the past two weeks, so Fehoko suddenly finds himself in a position to contribute. Fehoko played double-digit snaps for the first time in 2026 on Sunday, coincidentally against his former teams the Cowboys. He wasn't much of a factor in a comeback win, however, earning just one target for a 17-yard reception while taking the field for 40 of the team's 81 offensive play. While Fehoko could see his playing time climb even higher in Week 9, tight ends Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins, wideout Michael Wilson (ribs) and running back Tyler Allgeier may be better bets to command targets from quarterback Gardner Minshew.
injuryReports.injury: Fehoko is listed as a starting receiver on the Cardinals' unofficial depth chart heading into Sunday's game at Seattle, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.

injuryReports.name: James Conner
injuryReports.returnComment: Though LaFleur said last week that Conner could "potentially" play this season, that won't happen in Week 9. The veteran running back continues to work his way back from a right foot injury and has not yet been cleared to practice. Arizona is dealing with multiple injuries in its backfield, including Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion), so Conner could provide a big boost once he's able to work his way back this week. Instead, the team will turn to Tyler Allgeier to lead its backfield, with Evan Hull serving as his primary backup if Knight is unable to suit up Sunday against Seattle.
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Harrison Wallace III
injuryReports.returnComment: Wallace signed to Arizona's practice squad in August and has yet to play in a regular-season game. Week 9 will be the undrafted free agent's NFL debut should he be active for Sunday's matchup against Seattle. He will likely act as a depth piece should he play.
injuryReports.injury: The Cardinals signed Wallace from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.

injuryReports.name: Jeremiyah Love
injuryReports.returnComment: Love's move to IR was fully expected, after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported earlier Tuesday that the rookie first-round pick was diagnosed with a right high-ankle sprain and was facing a projected recovery timeline of 4-to-5 weeks. While Love is on the mend, Tyler Allgeier is expected to step into a lead role out of the Arizona backfield beginning with the team's Week 9 game against Seattle.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Kendrick Bourne
injuryReports.returnComment: Though Bourne is expected to avoid surgery after fracturing his right tibia during Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys, he's facing an expected recovery timeline of three months that effectively ends his season. With Bourne heading to IR, the Cardinals signed Harrison Wallace off their practice squad to replenish their depth at receiver. The 31-year-old Bourne will finish the 2026 campaign with 26 receptions for 263 yards and no touchdowns on 38 targets over eight appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Lower Leg

injuryReports.name: Nick Folk
injuryReports.returnComment: Folk registered multiple field-goal attempts for just the second time in four weeks, and he missed a field-goal try for the second straight week. The 42-year-old was able to convert a 31-yard attempt in the first quarter before pulling a 38-yard try wide left in the fourth quarter. The miss was Folk's first miss from inside 40 yards in a regular-season contest since 2017, snapping a streak of 107 straight makes from within that range.
injuryReports.injury: Folk went 1-for-2 on field-goal tries and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Zachariah Branch
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
injuryReports.returnComment: It was another quiet performance from Pitts, who hasn't reached 25 receiving yards in any of the last three games, and he had to watch backup tight end Charlie Woerner catch Michael Penix's only TD pass of the afternoon in the first quarter. Pitts will take a 25-220-4 line on 37 targets through nine contests into a Week 10 clash with Kansas City.
injuryReports.injury: Pitts caught three of five targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Michael Penix Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: It looked like it would be a big day for the Falcons offense when Penix led his team to points on its first two drives. including a one-yard TD to Charlie Woerner, but Atlanta managed just seven more points over the final three quarters. The touchdown pass was Penix's 10th of the season, setting a new career high, but he's also been picked off five times in the last two games after throwing only one INT in his first five contests of 2026. He'll face a tough test in Week 10 against Kansas City.
injuryReports.injury: Penix completed 20 of 31 passes for 162 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 34-17 loss to Cincinnati. He added 50 rushing yards on three carries.

injuryReports.name: Drake London
injuryReports.returnComment: Cincinnati's secondary did a good job of limiting London's looks from Michael Penix, but the fifth-year wideout still led Atlanta in receiving yards, although Bijan Robinson caught one more pass and Charlie Woerner hauled in the QB's only touchdown. London has gotten only 11 targets over the last two games, turning them into a disappointing 6-76-0 line, and he could have a hard time breaking out in Week 10 against a stingy Kansas City secondary.
injuryReports.injury: London caught all five of his targets for 68 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Bijan Robinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Backup Khalil Herbert handled just three touches, as Robinson dominated the workload in the Atlanta backfield with his usual No. 2, Brian Robinson (hamstring), on the shelf. It was the first time since Week 4 that Bijan had reached the century mark in rushing yards, and also the first time since that game against the Saints he got into the end zone. Robinson will look to build upon this effort in Week 10 against Kansas City.
injuryReports.injury: Robinson carried the ball 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and caught six of seven targets for 47 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.

injuryReports.name: Olamide Zaccheaus
injuryReports.returnComment: Zaccheaus was pulled from the game in the third quarter to be evaluated for a concussion. He cleared protocol relatively quickly and returned during the same period. He'll try to help Atlanta's offense rally back from a fourth-quarter deficit.
injuryReports.injury: Zaccheaus (head) has returned to Sunday's matchup against Cincinnati in Madrid, Spain, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Yasir Abdullah
injuryReports.returnComment: Abdullah was placed on injured reserve Oct. 10 due to a hamstring injury, and after missing the required four games while on the list, he was designated to return Wednesday and then activated Saturday, setting him up for his first game action since Week 4. A rotational role off the edge is likely for Abdullah due to James Pearce (back) making his season debut and all of Cameron Thomas, Za'Darius Smith and Charles Snowden available to the defense.
injuryReports.injury: Abdullah (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game versus the Bengals in Madrid, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: James Pearce Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Pearce completed his eight-game suspension for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy this week, but after being listed as a full participant on the Falcons' first two Week 9 injury reports, he was limited by a back injury Friday and thus entered the weekend as questionable to play. With his status now clarified for Sunday's matchup, he seems likely to resume his role as one of Atlanta's top pass rushers, which equated to 10.5 sacks among his 26 tackles in 17 regular-season games as a first-round rookie in 2025.
injuryReports.injury: Pearce (back) is listed as active Sunday versus the Bengals in Madrid, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Divine Deablo
injuryReports.returnComment: Since suffering a forearm injury during a Week 6 loss to the Bears, Deablo has missed the last two contests, and while he capped Week 9 prep with a questionable designation, his full session Friday signaled that he was closing in on a return to action. With that confirmed, he's a good bet to retake one of the starting inside linebacker spots in the Falcons defense, despite Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins holding down the fort in Deablo's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Deablo (forearm) is active for Sunday's game against the Bengals in Madrid, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Beaux Collins
injuryReports.returnComment: On cutdown day Aug. 30, the Falcons placed Collins on IR with a designation to return, which would have allowed him to practice as early as Week 3 prep. Instead, his hip injury kept him out of drills until Week 7, when his 21-day window opened, but he sat out the last two games before Atlanta finally activated him Saturday. With Zachariah Branch sidelined Sunday due to a hamstring issue, Collins will serve as a reserve WR along with Chris Blair behind Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus.
injuryReports.injury: Collins (hip) is listed as active Sunday against the Bengals in Madrid, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Cameron Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams was designated to return to practice Oct. 22 and logged a trio of full practices this week. However, the Falcons have elected against activating him ahead of Sunday's game. If Atlanta doesn't activate Williams by next Thursday, he'll be required to miss the remainder of the campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Khalil Herbert
injuryReports.returnComment: Herbert was elevated for both Week 7 and Week 8, turning six carries into 21 yards and two catches (on two targets) into 22 yards while also working as a kick returner. He could take on a bigger role Sunday versus Cincinnati and potentially beyond, as No. 2 RB Brian Robinson was placed on injured reserve Saturday due to a hamstring injury. That means Herbert is the Falcons' only healthy running back behind workhorse Bijan Robinson
injuryReports.injury: The Falcons signed Herbert from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Robinson already has missed two games due to a lingering hamstring injury and now must miss at least the next four outings, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 13 at Cleveland. In a corresponding move, the Falcons are signing Khalil Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster to continue serving as the No. 2 RB behind workhorse Bijan Robinson.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Samson Ebukam
injuryReports.returnComment: Ebukam suffered a hamstring injury in Week 9 versus the Buccaneers, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result of the injury. In his absence, Za'Darius Smith is a top candidate to operate in a more prominent role at outside linebacker.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Chris Blair
injuryReports.returnComment: Blair has been active for all eight of the Falcons' games this season, but the 29-year-old wideout has been scarcely involved on offense. He's thus far recorded just a six-yard reception on four targets, three of which came in Week 2. Blair should continue to suit up for the Falcons on gamedays but will provide most of his value on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Blair went without a target while playing nine of the Falcons' 53 offensive snaps in Sunday's 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers.

injuryReports.name: Jahan Dotson
injuryReports.returnComment: Dotson and the rest of the Falcons offense were held in check for the majority of Sunday's loss. The wide receiver did provide Atlanta's biggest highlight play of the day, connecting with quarterback Michael Penix for a 76-yard gain on the team's final possession of the day in the fourth quarter. Dotson's 95 yards were a season high, and he has now reeled in 14 of 31 targets for 337 yards and two touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.
injuryReports.injury: Dotson caught two of five targets for 95 yards during Sunday's 16-0 loss to Tampa Bay.

injuryReports.name: Avieon Terrell
injuryReports.returnComment: Terrell didn't play in Week 8 versus the 49ers, his first absence of the 2026 campaign. He practiced in a limited capacity during the week but still couldn't avoid a questionable designation for the divisional meeting with the Buccaneers. However, Terrell now has the green light to return from the one-game layoff, which will likely result in less work for C.J. Henderson (groin) and Mike Ford.
injuryReports.injury: Terrell (back/illness) is active for Sunday's game against Tampa Bay.

injuryReports.name: Anterio Thompson
injuryReports.returnComment: It's an awful situation for Thompson, who had been set for a chance to play in the NFL after being selected by the Falcons in the sixth round of April's draft. Atlanta has not said much about Thompson, who currently resides on the team's reserve/non-football injury list.
injuryReports.injury: Undisclosed

injuryReports.name: Jaylinn Hawkins
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Nate Wiggins
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Jacoby Brissett
injuryReports.returnComment: Brissett officially landed with the Ravens in a trade with the Cardinals this past Friday, and he's now on track to assume his new team's starting QB role for the foreseeable future. As a result, Joe Fagnano -- who had a spot start in Week 9 -- will revert to backup status. With regard to franchise signal-caller Lamar Jackson (thumb), who currently is on IR, he's indicated that he plans to return later this season. However, he's out for at least three more games, and 4-5 Baltimore's record as the season progresses figures to factor into Jackson's approach to a potential return to action.
injuryReports.injury: Ahead of Week 10, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter noted "I expect (Brissett) to be our starter" next Monday against the Chargers, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Lamar Jackson
injuryReports.returnComment: Jackson dislocated and fractured his right thumb on his only play of last Sunday's loss at Buffalo, and while he was placed on injured reserve Thursday, he hasn't been ruled out for the season. Considering the typical recovery for his particular injury is in the 6-to-9-week range, per Rapoport, Jackson has a chance to return before the end of the regular season, but the Ravens will need to stay in the playoff hunt. To that end, Baltimore obtained Jacoby Brissett from Arizona this week to bolster a QB room that not only lost Jackson indefinitely but also Tyler Huntley for the season due to a turf-toe injury. Brissett's experience gives the team a chance to get back to winning ways after losing four games in a row.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Malaki Starks
injuryReports.returnComment: Starks tied for third on his team in tackles during a rather uninspiring performance on both offense and defense by the Ravens. He did make a big play when he forced a fumble that was recovered by Baltimore in the third quarter, but the Ravens turned the ball over on downs on four plays on their ensuing possession. Starks logged 84 tackles over 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year, and he's well on his way to surpassing that mark with 55 stops (including 1.0 sacks) through nine contests in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Starks finished Baltimore's Week 9 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday with four tackles (three solo) and a forced fumble.

injuryReports.name: Roquan Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith led his team in tackles on a night when Baltimore had a hard time slowing down the Jaguars' offense. Though he's been bothered by knee and foot issues in recent weeks, the veteran linebacker logged a 95 percent defensive snap share Thursday. Smith is well on his way to another triple-digit tackle campaign with 74 stops, including 2.0 sacks, along with an interception and two forced fumbles through nine contests.
injuryReports.injury: Smith finished with eight tackles (two solo) in Thursday's Week 9 loss to Jacksonville.

injuryReports.name: Derrick Henry
injuryReports.returnComment: With Baltimore sitting at 4-5 and having lost its top two QBs in Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) for the foreseeable future and rest of the season, respectively, there has been speculation Henry may be available via trade, but the team has informed the running back that it doesn't intend to consider such a transaction. Instead, the Ravens have dealt for quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals to help stabilize the offense, which may help Henry end his streak being held under 100 yards rushing at four contests. Overall, Henry has racked up 689 yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries for a career-low 3.9 YPC in his nine appearances in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: The Ravens aren't expected to deal Henry before Tuesday's trade deadline, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Matt Hibner
injuryReports.returnComment: Hibner ranked second among Baltimore tight ends with 30 offensive snaps, just behind Mark Andrews (32). The former didn't do much with the opportunity, but it was a very quiet game for the Ravens' passing game as a whole, as starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Baltimore will likely have the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett starting behind center for the team's next game (Monday, Oct. 16 versus the Chargers), but Hibner has just six catches across eight contests this season, so he's not a viable fantasy option regardless of who is throwing him the ball.
injuryReports.injury: Hibner logged one reception for five yards on two targets in Thursday's loss to Baltimore.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
injuryReports.returnComment: Lane logged 32 offensive snaps, third-most among Baltimore wideouts behind Zay Flowers (37) and Rashod Bateman (35). However, Lane failed to haul in a pass (and to even see a target) for the first time this season. That can be partly attributed to quarterback play, as Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore recently traded for, will likely start behind center in Week 10 against the Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16, which would improve Lane's outlook to some degree. However, he's caught one or fewer passes in three of his five games so far this season, so Lane isn't a recommended fantasy play regardless of who is starting at QB for Baltimore.
injuryReports.injury: Lane did not draw a target Thursday in a loss to Jacksonville.

injuryReports.name: Jake Moody
injuryReports.returnComment: Moody made his only field-goal try and converted his only extra-point attempt during Thursday's 33-10 loss versus the Jaguars. Regular starting kicker Tyler Loop (groin) is not eligible to return from injured reserve until after the Ravens' bye in Week 13, so the team is expected to either sign Moody to its active roster or elevate him again ahead of its Week 10 matchup versus the Chargers.
injuryReports.injury: Moody reverted to Baltimore's practice squad Friday, per the NFL's transaction log.

injuryReports.name: Josh Cuevas
injuryReports.returnComment: Cuevas split time with nine snaps on both offense and special teams. This game marked the fourth time this season that the rookie had zero targets. Prior to Thursday night, the 23-year-old saw multiple targets in four straight games. He will likely have a similar role as the season continues.
injuryReports.injury: Cuevas didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Devontez Walker
injuryReports.returnComment: Walker made little impact in Thursday night's loss, playing 15 offensive snaps behind Ja'Kobi Lane (32), Rashod Bateman (35) and Zay Flowers (37). Walker will likely see a similar role as the season progresses.
injuryReports.injury: Walker didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Rashod Bateman
injuryReports.returnComment: That's back-to-back one-catch games for Bateman with Joe Fagnano at quarterback for the Ravens. With Zay Flowers also healthy, Bateman has little fantasy appeal in season-long formats, though things could change when Jacoby Brissett takes over as Baltimore's starting quarterback in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Bateman caught one of two targets for six yards in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Justice Hill
injuryReports.returnComment: Hill provided the sole offensive highlight of the night for the moribund, Joe Fagnano-led offense, making one cut after getting the handoff from the rookie quarterback halfway through the fourth quarter and bursting through the defense up the right side of the field for a 65-yard touchdown run. Hill's yardage total was both a team- and season-high figure for the veteran change-of-pace back, who should benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals whenever the veteran signal-caller is able to take the reins of the offense.
injuryReports.injury: Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for seven yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Mark Andrews
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran tight end actually led the Ravens in receiving yards with his modest total, as fill-in signal-caller Joe Fagnano averaged just 3.3 yards per attempt and totaled 60 passing yards overall. Andrews opened the season with back-to-back 49-yard tallies on 10 total catches, but he's been stuck at 28 receiving yards or fewer in his seven subsequent games. Andrews will hope to benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett, who should bring some stability and productivity to Baltimore's currently embattled quarterback situation.
injuryReports.injury: Andrews secured both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Joe Fagnano
injuryReports.returnComment: Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) on injured reserve, and the undrafted rookie signal-caller unsurprisingly had a difficult night after also struggling in emergency duty against the Bills just four days earlier. Fagnano had been dealing with an ankle injury stemming from his aforementioned NFL debut and had little practice time on a short week, so offensive coordinator Declan Doyle kept the game plan simple and focused on the short areas of the field, resulting in Fagnano averaging just 3.3 yards per attempt. Both of Fagnano's second-half picks also led to Jacksonville field goals, making it a forgettable night overall. With the Ravens reportedly putting the finishing touches on a trade with the Cardinals for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, Fagnano is likely to move into a reserve role as soon as a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.
injuryReports.injury: Fagnano completed 10 of 18 passes for 60 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions while adding three rushes for 13 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Zay Flowers
injuryReports.returnComment: Joe Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (IR, thumb) and Tyler Huntley (IR, toe) out of action, and the rookie undrafted signal-caller averaged a microscopic 3.3 yards per attempt and threw two interceptions. Therefore, Flowers once again put forth a forgettable receiving line, although he at least got on the board with a trio of catches after being blanked on five targets in the Week 8 loss to the Bills. The Ravens tried to boost Flowers' touches with his trio of rush attempts, and he was reasonably effective with those. While fantasy managers have gotten next to nothing from the talented receiver over the last two games, Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore is finalizing a trade for with the Cardinals, could be ready to suit up as soon as a Week 10 home matchup with the Chargers on Monday night, Nov. 16.
injuryReports.injury: Flowers brought in three of six targets for six yards and rushed three times for 17 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Hamilton
injuryReports.returnComment: Hamilton tweaked his hip late in the first half, and after he was able to play through it briefly early in the second half, he has now been ruled out for the rest of the team's Week 9 matchup. The 25-year-old will now shift his focus to being ready for the team's Week 10 contest against the Chargers on Nov. 16. In Hamilton's absence, Keyon Martin is a top candidate to see an increase in opportunities in Baltimore's secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Hip

injuryReports.name: Adisa Isaac
injuryReports.returnComment: Isaac is nursing a hamstring injury, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. The linebacker operates primarily as a special-teams option, so his absence doesn't have any impact on Baltimore's defensive approach.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Tyler Huntley
injuryReports.returnComment: Huntley and Lamar Jackson (thumb) were both placed on injured reserve Thursday. The latter still has at least a slim chance to return this season, while Huntley's injury has been confirmed to be season-ending. Joe Fagnano is set to start Thursday's game against the Jaguars before reinforcements arrive under center in the form of Jacoby Brissett, for whom the Ravens are expected to finalize a trade over the weekend.
injuryReports.injury: Toe

injuryReports.name: Adam Randall
injuryReports.returnComment: Randall was not considered to be limited during Baltimore's walkthrough practice Wednesday but he's still on IR going into game-day. If he's not activated for Week 9, his next opportunity to make his regular-season debut would come in Week 10 versus the Chargers.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Damar Hamlin
injuryReports.returnComment: Hamlin is back in the game after having briefly exited while dealing with cramping. Geno Stone had replaced Hamlin at safety while he was sidelined.
injuryReports.injury: Hamlin (leg) has returned to Buffalo's matchup versus the Vikings on Monday, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.

injuryReports.name: Christian Benford
injuryReports.returnComment: Benford was briefly sidelined with a wrist injury late in the first half, but he has now returned to the field following the break. He will continue to be tasked with attempting to slow down Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison on the other side.
injuryReports.injury: Benford (wrist) has returned to Monday night's matchup with Minnesota.

injuryReports.name: Joshua Palmer
injuryReports.returnComment: ir
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Dion Dawkins
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Ribs

injuryReports.name: Greg Gaines
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Alec Anderson
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Tyrell Shavers
injuryReports.returnComment: Shavers will remain sidelined for at least one more game as he continues to work his way back from a torn ACL. The wide receiver returned to practice in late October, and he could be activated prior to the team's Week 10 matchup with the Jets.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - ACL

injuryReports.name: Jalon Kilgore
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Mike Danna
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Skyler Bell
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Trent Sherfield
injuryReports.returnComment: While Buffalo has a healthy receiving corps, Sherfield was elevated to bolster depth at the position. The 30-year-old was last active in Week 5 against the Rams. However, he didn't draw a target and spent most of his time on special teams. That could be the case again Monday versus the Vikings.
injuryReports.injury: Sherfield was elevated to the 53-man roster off the practice squad ahead of Monday's game against Minnesota.

injuryReports.name: Spencer Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Brown missed last Sunday's win over Baltimore, but he'll be back in action Monday after logging an LP/LP/FP practice progression this week. His return will be especially critical if fellow starting offensive tackle Dion Dawkins (ribs, questionable) isn't able to suit up.
injuryReports.injury: Brown (back) does not have a designation for Monday's matchup in Minnesota.

injuryReports.name: Keon Coleman
injuryReports.returnComment: Per Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News, Coleman again was spotted in a red non-contact jersey Saturday and eventually went down as a limited participant for a third consecutive practice. Despite the restrictions this week, though, Coleman is ready to suit up for an eighth straight game to begin the season, having put up a 20-287-3 line on 27 targets to date.
injuryReports.injury: Coleman (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's contest in Minnesota.

injuryReports.name: DJ Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: While logging three straight limited practices during Week 9 prep, Moore continued to wear a red non-contact jersey due to the AC joint sprain that he's been dealing with since Week 2. Now that he's in the clear for Monday's matchup, he'll look to build upon the 16-260-2 line on 27 targets that he's racked up through five eppearances on the campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Moore (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's contest at Minnesota.

injuryReports.name: Ty Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: A quick return after Thursday's absence confirms Johnson isn't dealing with a serious illness. He should be fine for his usual role on passing downs Monday night at Minnesota.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson (illness) was a full practice participant Friday.

injuryReports.name: Dalton Kincaid
injuryReports.returnComment: Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo previously noted that Kincaid had shed his red non-contact jersey at Friday's practice, and the tight end's full participation in the session paves the way for him to be in uniform Monday night against the Vikings. Over his last two games, Kincaid (who overall is tied for first among Bills in catches (27) and leads the team in receiving yards (401)) has logged an 11-124-1 receiving line, a pace that keeps him relevant from a fantasy perspective.
injuryReports.injury: Kincaid (chest) was a full participant in Friday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Dee Alford
injuryReports.returnComment: Alford was inactive for Sunday's win over the Ravens, though it appears he will be back on the field when the Bills face the Vikings on Monday night. With the 28-year-old back in the equation, Te'Cory Couch and Maxwell Hairston will likely see fewer snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Alford (ankle) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Hancock
injuryReports.returnComment: Hancock has been on IR since late September while recovering from a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 2 versus Detroit. The cornerback had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, and if he isn't activated in that time frame, he will remain on IR for the rest of the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Dawson Knox
injuryReports.returnComment: It's a typical receiving line for Knox, whose main contributions come in the blocking department. Knox has nine grabs for 42 yards and one touchdown across seven appearances this season. He'd likely need multiple wideout and tight-end injuries to be a fantasy consideration.
injuryReports.injury: Knox caught one of two targets for six yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Ray Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: With the Bills throttling the Ravens and James Cook suffering a neck injury late in the game, Davis got some added run in the fourth quarter. If Cook misses any time, Davis would be the likely early-down replacement, with Ty Johnson sticking to his role on passing downs and four- and two-minute situations.
injuryReports.injury: Davis rushed six times for 30 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Bass
injuryReports.returnComment: Bass converted multiple long-range field goals for the Bills after the offense stalled several times due to drops. The kicker succeeded from 56 yards, 22 yards and 51 yards in the contest. Bass has converted all 16 of his field-goal attempts and is 21-for-23 on PATs through seven games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Bass made all three of his field-goal attempts as well as three PATs in the Bills' 36-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Greg Dortch
injuryReports.returnComment: Dortch has been serving as Buffalo's top return man throughout the season, but he continues to see limited involvement as a receiver. The 28-year-old hasn't played more than five offensive snaps in any of his seven appearances and has yet to draw a target.
injuryReports.injury: Dortch went without a target while logging four of the Bills' 82 snaps on offense in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. He returned one kickoff for 22 yards and three punts for 40 yards.

injuryReports.name: Khalil Shakir
injuryReports.returnComment: Shakir initially appeared to get in the end zone for a six-yard touchdown early in the first quarter, but he was ruled out at the one-yard line after review. Josh Allen then punched in the one-yard touchdown two plays later. On the day, Shakir paced the Bills with his five grabs and tied for second on the team in targets, one behind DJ Moore. Shakir has yet to hit 100 yards in a game this season and has just one touchdown, settling in as a low-ceiling WR4 in fantasy, especially when both Moore and Dalton Kincaid are healthy.
injuryReports.injury: Shakir caught five of six targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
injuryReports.returnComment: Fitzgerald went without a field-goal make for the second time in three weeks, and he pushed his only field-goal attempt of the day wide right from 43 yards in the second quarter. The miss was his first on a field-goal try this year, and the kicker has now gone 13-for-14 on field-goal attempts, including 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards, while making 16 of 21 extra-point attempts over eight regular-season contests so far.
injuryReports.injury: Fitzgerald missed his only field-goal attempt and went 3-for-3 on extra-point tries during Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Jaycee Horn
injuryReports.returnComment: Horn has had a productive NFL career, amassing 196 total tackles (139 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and 10 interceptions across 56 regular-season games over six seasons. He underwent surgery on his quad back in September. However, until Horn is back on the field or there is a more informative update, he should be considered week-to-week.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Mike Jackson
injuryReports.returnComment: Jackson underwent core-muscle surgery in September and has been on injured reserve to this point in the season. While he was expected to be evaluated after eight weeks, there haven't been any real updates regarding his return to the field. The 2019 No. 158 overall pick has appeared in 74 regular-season games during his career, accruing 262 total tackles (209 solo), one forced fumble, two fumble recoveries and one touchdown.
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Ja'Tavion Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: Sanders was active for the first time this season. However, he didn't log any offensive snaps and spent all his time on special teams. The 23-year-old has appeared in 30 regular-season games during his career, amassing 62 catches (77 targets) for 532 yards and two touchdowns. Sanders has had a few quality performances throughout his short NFL career, though he likely won't have an opportunity to get involved offensively moving ahead while Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller are in the mix.
injuryReports.injury: Sanders recorded zero targets during Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Jaelan Phillips
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Will Lee III
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Damien Lewis
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Bobby Okereke
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Foot

injuryReports.name: Xavier Legette
injuryReports.returnComment: Carolina will likely wait until it holds its first Week 10 practice Wednesday before officially opening Legette's 21-day evaluation window. The third-year receiver hasn't played since Sept. 20 due to the knee injury, so he may need to turn in multiple full practices this week to put himself in a position to return from IR ahead of this Sunday's game against the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jonathon Brooks
injuryReports.returnComment: Brooks, who remains on IR, was seen working off to the side during the Panthers' unofficial practice last Tuesday, per Joe Person of The Athletic, perhaps signaling some progress for the oft-injured RB, who last saw game action in Week 2. In Brooks' absence, Chuba Hubbard has dominated Carolina's backfield touches.
injuryReports.injury: Abdomen

injuryReports.name: Jalen Coker
injuryReports.returnComment: It was yet another quiet game from Coker, who has been held below 40 receiving yards in four of the last five games. Since his massive 8-138-2 receiving line in Week 1, Coker has averaged just 3.8 catches for 65.5 receiving yards per game over his last six contests. He has only one touchdown during that span. Coker will be in a bounce-back spot against the Saints at the Superdome next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Coker caught four of five targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Tommy Tremble
injuryReports.returnComment: The Panthers continue to use three tight ends heavily on offense, and Tremble has settled in as the do-it-all tight member of the trio, while Darren Waller is solely a pass catcher and Mitchell Evans focuses on blocking. Tremble doesn't have nearly the upside of Waller, but the former still draws Bryce Young's eye in the red zone. On the year, Tremble is up to 21 grabs for 179 yards and three touchdowns on 30 targets across eight games. He's not an exciting fantasy option.
injuryReports.injury: Tremble caught four of six targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Darren Waller
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran tight end was Bryce Young's favorite option on the afternoon, leading the Panthers in catches, targets and receiving yards, and Waller was on the other end of a 15-yard TD strike from the QB in the third quarter. It was Waller's most productive game since he returned from a brief retirement last season, and through eight games in 2026 he's put together a 23-299-4 line on 35 targets. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 against the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Waller caught eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Tetairoa McMillan
injuryReports.returnComment: The second-year wideout caught Bryce Young's third TD of the afternoon, a four-yard toss late in the fourth quarter that gave the Panthers some late hope. It was McMillan's first trip to the end zone since Week 4, and through eight games he's collected a 46-625-3 line on 71 targets. He'll look to build on this performance in a Week 10 road trip to New Orleans.
injuryReports.injury: McMillan caught four of six targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.

injuryReports.name: Chuba Hubbard
injuryReports.returnComment: The 27-year-old RB nearly produced 100-plus scrimmage yards for the fifth time in the last six games but fell just short. Hubbard remains on track for a career-best campaign, and through eight games he's delivered 619 yards and five TDs on the ground while adding a 26-167-2 line on 31 targets. He lines up for a juicy matchup in Week 10 against the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Hubbard carried the ball 16 times for 79 yards and caught four of five targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 26-21 loss to Denver.

injuryReports.name: Bryce Young
injuryReports.returnComment: The fourth-year QB tossed TDs in each of the last three quarters, finding Tommy Tremble, Darren Waller and Tetairoa McMillan, but Young's attempt to engineer a game-winning drive inside the final two minutes ended on a Nik Bonitto strip sack. It's the third time this season Young has thrown three touchdowns, but his first such performance since Week 2. He'll take a 16:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Saints.
injuryReports.injury: Young completed 28 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. He added 13 yards on his only carry and lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Torricelli Simpkins III
injuryReports.returnComment: Simpkins didn't suit up in the Week 8 loss to Green Bay due to an ankle injury, though it won't keep him off the field again for Sunday's meeting with the Broncos.
injuryReports.injury: Simpkins (ankle) is available for Sunday's game against Denver, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Corey Bullock
injuryReports.returnComment: Bullock was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. However, after logging full sessions Thursday and Friday, he is good to go for Week 9.
injuryReports.injury: Bullock (quadriceps) is active for Sunday's game versus Denver, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Brady Christensen
injuryReports.returnComment: Christensen has been on injured reserve since Sept. 1. He was designated to return Tuesday and was a full participant in all three of Carolina's practices this week, but the Panthers aren't ready to activate him. Christensen's next chance to play is Sunday, Nov. 15, in New Orleans.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Marco Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson was elevated for the first time this season last weekend, and he ended up starting and logging every Panthers defensive snap against Green Bay. The veteran cornerback could do the same Sunday versus Denver, as Will Lee has been ruled out due to a hamstring injury and Akayleb Evans (triceps) is on IR. Wilson finished with eight tackles and two defensed passes in his Panthers debut.
injuryReports.injury: The Panthers elevated Wilson from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Bobby Brown III
injuryReports.returnComment: Brown missed last Thursday night's loss to the Packers but appears ready to return for Sunday's Week 9 date with Denver. He has seven tackles (one solo) and a pass breakup across 142 defensive snaps this season.
injuryReports.injury: Brown (hand) practiced fully Wednesday.

injuryReports.name: Zakee Wheatley
injuryReports.returnComment: Wheatley was able to secure a career-high seven stops, while his biggest play of the game came in the fourth quarter when he picked off a deep pass from Packers quarterback Jordan Love. The interception was the first of the Wheatley's career, and the rookie has now compiled 26 total tackles (19 solo), four passes defensed and a forced fumble over six contests during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Wheatley recorded seven total tackles (four solo) and an interception during Thursday night's 27-19 loss to the Packers.

injuryReports.name: Samaje Perine
injuryReports.returnComment: Perine logged two more carries than Chase Brown in the game, but Brown out produced him with 57 rushing yards. Perine has continued to operate in a prominent role as the Bengals' No. 2 option in the backfield, and he would stand to be a rather valuable fantasy asset in the case that Brown is forced to miss any action down the road this season.
injuryReports.injury: Perine rushed 11 times for 43 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Kyle Dugger
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: Andrei Iosivas
injuryReports.returnComment: Cincinnati has yet to open Iosivas' 21-day practice window since he landed on IR on Sept. 26, so until that happens, the wideout's return to game action shouldn't be considered imminent. While Iosivas has been sidelined for the Bengals' past six games, Dohnte Meyers has been serving as the primary No. 3 wideout behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, and tight end Mike Gesicki has also benefited from an expanded profile in the passing attack.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Evan McPherson
injuryReports.returnComment: McPherson was able to convert multiple field-goal tries in a game for the first time since Week 3, nailing a 57-yarder in the final moments of the first half before later adding a 43-yard make in the fourth quarter. The kicker had gone back-to-back games without a field-goal attempt, but he has now gone a perfect 12-for-12 on field-goal tries, including 6-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests this season.
injuryReports.injury: McPherson went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts while making all four of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Mike Gesicki
injuryReports.returnComment: Gesicki entered Week 9 having scored a touchdown in five straight games, and he saw his streak come to an end Sunday. The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week and fifth time this season, but his 11 receiving yards left much to be desired. Gesicki has now reeled in 19 of 26 targets for 252 yards and six touchdowns over eight regular-season games so far this year.
injuryReports.injury: Gesicki caught both of his targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win versus Atlanta.

injuryReports.name: Chase Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Samaje Perine actually saw more volume on the ground with 11 carries for 43 yards, but most of his workload came in the fourth quarter as the Bengals were grinding down the clock. Brown has yet to top 80 rushing yards in a game this season and he hasn't gotten into the end zone since Week 1, a disappointing first half of the year for a running back who amassed at least 1,300 scrimmage yards with double-digit scores each of the prior two campaigns. Brown will look for an opportunity to break out in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Brown carried the ball nine times for 57 yards and caught all three of his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Tee Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: While he didn't see big volume, Higgins made his opportunities count, connecting with Joe Burrow on a four-yard TD in the second quarter and an eight-yard score in the third. Higgins has hit paydirt five times in the last three games, and on the season he's produced a 48-758-6 line on 67 targets through eight contests. He'll look to extend his scoring streak in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North clash with the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins caught five of six targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over Atlanta.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Marr Chase
injuryReports.returnComment: The superstar wideout hit the ground running in Madrid, capping Cincinnati's first drive with a 47-yard touchdown catch from Joe Burrow. It was Chase's fourth straight game getting into the end zone, a stretch in which he's delivered a stellar 32-435-4 line on 45 targets, and Sunday's 155 receiving yards were a season high. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Chase caught 10 of 12 targets for 155 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Joe Burrow
injuryReports.returnComment: It was a nearly flawless performance from Burrow, as he hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score in the first quarter and tossed a pair of shorter TDs to Tee Higgins later in the contest. The superstar QB also got into the end zone on a goal-line sneak in the second quarter. It's the fourth straight game in which Burrow has produced at least four touchdowns, an incredible stretch in which he's completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 1,215 yards with a 16:3 TD:INT plus two more scores on the ground. The Bengals, not coincidentally, are 4-0 in that span. Burrow will look to stay locked in for a big AFC North clash against the Steelers in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. He added seven yards and a TD on three carries.

injuryReports.name: Cedric Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson suffered an ankle injury last Sunday versus the Titans, and he subsequently followed a DNP/LP/FP practice regimen during Week 9 prep before getting a questionable designation ahead of Sunday's international matchup. Now that he's confirmed to be active, he should be good for his normal 20-30 percent weekly defensive snap share.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson (ankle) is listed as active Sunday against the Falcons in Madrid.

injuryReports.name: DJ Turner II
injuryReports.returnComment: Turner was injured in last Sunday's overtime win against the Titans and was unable to return. He avoided a serious injury and will be ready to do battle with Drake London in Spain on Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Turner (ankle) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Cashius Howell
injuryReports.returnComment: Howell suffered a right wrist injury during Sunday's overtime win against the Titans, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result. The defensive lineman has already undergone surgery, per Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com, and in Howell's absence, Shemar Stewart will stand to see an increase in workload at defensive end.
injuryReports.injury: Wrist

injuryReports.name: Colbie Young
injuryReports.returnComment: Though quarterback Joe Burrow set season highs in passing yards (462) and passing touchdowns (five), Young didn't see any involvement while the targets were highly concentrated among Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown. The fourth-round pick out of Georgia has held a bit role so far during his rookie season, recording two catches for nine yards on two targets through five appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Young went without a target while playing 19 of the Bengals' 74 snaps on offense in Sunday's 43-36 overtime win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Erick All Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: All, who sustained the injury in Sunday's win over the Ravens, has now torn the ACL in his right knee three times during his career. He first tore the ACL during his final collegiate season at Iowa in 2023, then had his 2024 rookie campaign with the Bengals cut short after damaging the ligament again. Given the timing of the injury along with the fact that he'll be working his way back from a third surgery of the same knee, All is far from guaranteed to be ready to play when the 2027 season gets underway.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - ACL

injuryReports.name: Barrett Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter didn't play every defensive snap for just the first time this season, but his nine stops were tied with Bryan Cook for most on the Bengals. Carter has logged at least five stops in each of the first six games of the regular season and is up to 50 tackles (22 solo), including 1.5 sacks, three pass defenses and one forced fumble in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Carter recorded nine tackles (three solo) and a pass defense during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Boye Mafe
injuryReports.returnComment: Mafe got to Tyler Huntley for a six-yard sack midway through the first quarter before splitting another sack with Bryan Cook in the fourth. Mafe has logged at least 1.0 sacks in three consecutive games and is up to 4.5 sacks through six regular-season games, which already surpasses his total from 2025 with Seattle (2.0 sacks across 17 regular-season contests).
injuryReports.injury: Mafe finished Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens with five tackles (three solo), including 1.5 sacks.

injuryReports.name: Bryan Cook
injuryReports.returnComment: Cook and Boye Mafe combined for a split sack on Tyler Huntley midway through the fourth quarter, which was Cook's first sack since his rookie year in 2022. The fifth-year safety is up to 26 tackles (18 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through five regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Cook recorded nine tackles (six solo), including 0.5 sacks, during the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Demetrius Knight Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Knight finished third on the team in tackles behind Bryan Cook and Barrett Carter during the victory, in addition to snagging his first interception of the campaign. The 26-year-old continues to have a productive season, as he's now recorded seven or more tackles in five of his six appearances, bringing his total on the campaign to 50 (21 solo).
injuryReports.injury: Knight totaled eight tackles (two solo) and an interception during the Bengals' win over the Ravens on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Maliek Collins
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Elbow

injuryReports.name: Deshaun Watson
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Andre Szmyt
injuryReports.returnComment: Szmyt was able to convert multiple field-goal tries for the eighth straight game, and his three makes matched a season high for the 28-year-old. The kicker made a 41-yarder in the second quarter and a 30-yard attempt in the third quarter before tying the game up at 16-16 with a 51-yard make with eight seconds left in regulation. Szmyt has now gone 19-for-21 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Szmyt went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to New Orleans.

injuryReports.name: Jerry Jeudy
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran wideout had zero grabs headed into the Browns' finals drive of regulation, but a 30-yard grab down the left sideline followed up a by a seven-yard gain two plays later set Cleveland up for the game-tying field goal to send it to overtime. The fourth option in the passing attack for the Browns, Jeudy has 18 catches for 208 yards and no touchdowns through nine games this season. He's well off the fantasy radar.
injuryReports.injury: Jeudy caught two of four targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Dylan Sampson
injuryReports.returnComment: Sampson toted the rock a season-high eight times, but he averaged a minimal 2.6 yards per carry. The running back remained heavily involved in the passing game, tying wide receiver KC Concepcion for second on the team in targets behind wideout Denzel Boston (seven). Sampson has now reeled in three or more passes in three straight games, and he figures to remain most valuable as a pass catcher for fantasy managers ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup with Houston.
injuryReports.injury: Sampson rushed eight times for 21 yards while catching three of six targets for 27 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss against the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: With Shedeur Sanders under center for the first time in place of Deshaun Watson (concussion), Fannin did little in regulation as the second-year QB instead looked for rookie wideouts Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. Sanders went back to a more familiar target in OT, however, connecting with Fannin on a 39-yard TD in the extra frame that saw the tight end flatten a couple defenders with stiff arms on his way to the end zone. Fannin had a slow start to the season, but over the last three weeks he's amassed an 18-287-1 line on 23 targets, giving him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 10 clash with the Texans no matter who is throwing him passes.
injuryReports.injury: Fannin caught both his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints.

injuryReports.name: KC Concepcion
injuryReports.returnComment: Most of Concepcion's production came on a 64-yard TD in the fourth quarter as Shedeur Sanders found him just inside New Orleans' 30-yard line and the speedy rookie -- who briefly exited the contest after sustained what appeared to be a right leg issue -- to did the rest by eluding a couple defenders. It was Concepcion's first career NFL touchdown, and he sports a 37-437-1 line on 55 targets through his first nine games for the Browns. If Sanders takes over from Deshaun Watson (concussion) on a permanent basis, it could lead to plenty more big plays for Concepcion.
injuryReports.injury: Concepcion caught four of six targets for 85 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. He added three yards on his only carry.

injuryReports.name: Denzel Boston
injuryReports.returnComment: The 98 yards led the Browns on the afternoon, and Boston showed some immediate chemistry with Shedeur Sanders, connecting with the QB on a 60-yard strike in the third quarter that nearly resulted in a touchdown. The rookie receiver was also the target on a two-point conversion attempt that would have won the game in OT, but the pass got broken up. Boston also set a new career high in receiving yards with the performance, and if Sanders takes over for Deshaun Watson (concussion) under center on a permanent basis, it could lead to plenty more big plays. Through his first nine NFL games. Boston has delivered a 32-507-3 line on 61 targets.
injuryReports.injury: Boston caught six of seven targets for 98 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Quinshon Judkins
injuryReports.returnComment: The Browns' running game once again struggled, with the team averaging just 2.8 yards per carry overall, and Judkins' longest gain went for only 12 yards. Dylan Sampson saw a season-high 11 touches to Judkins' 16, and the backfield could be drifting toward a timeshare as coach Todd Monken looks for solutions. Judkins has topped 70 rushing yards in a game just once all season, and he seems unlikely to break out in a Week 10 meeting with the Texans.
injuryReports.injury: Judkins carried the ball 15 times for 43 yards and caught his only target for two yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints.

injuryReports.name: Shedeur Sanders
injuryReports.returnComment: Making his first start of the season in place of Deshaun Watson (concussion), Sanders put together an impressive performance, hitting KC Concepcion for a 64-yard TD late in the fourth quarter and then connecting with Harold Fannin for a 39-yard score in OT. Todd Monken elected to go for the win with a two-point conversion rather than giving the ball back to New Orleans, but Sanders' attempt to hit Denzel Boston in the corner of the end zone failed, although the play would have been wiped out by a holding call anyway. Even if Watson is deemed ready to go ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Texans, Sanders' strong showing may have given his coach something to think about.
injuryReports.injury: Sanders completed 19 of 31 passes for 297 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. He added 28 yards on 10 carries.

injuryReports.name: Michael Burton
injuryReports.returnComment: Burton exited due to a calf injury in the first half and was deemed questionable to return. However, he was able to return to action before halftime. Burton should thus continue to get occasional snaps at fullback while also helping out on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Burton (calf) has returned to Sunday's matchup against New Orleans, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Dillon Gabriel
injuryReports.returnComment: It was announced earlier in the week that Shedeur Sanders would start Sunday's contest due to Deshaun Watson being in concussion protocol, and although Watson has not officially been ruled out for Week 9 as of yet, he reportedly will be. That will leave the backup spot to Gabriel, but presumably for only one contest, as the report notes Watson is expected back for Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Gabriel "will serve as the backup quarterback" Sunday against the Saints, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Quincy Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams finished the week with back-to-back limited practices heading into Week 9 against the Saints. Williams has recorded 55 total tackles (32 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and four forced fumbles in eight games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Williams has no injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.

injuryReports.name: Malachi Corley
injuryReports.returnComment: For the fourth time in eight appearances, Corley logged double-digit snaps on offense, but the third-year receiver has yet to draw a target this season. He'll continue to provide most of his value to the Browns as a kickoff returner.
injuryReports.injury: Corley went untargeted while playing 13 of 70 snaps on offense Sunday in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers. He returned one kickoff for 26 yards.

injuryReports.name: Tylan Wallace
injuryReports.returnComment: The reception was Wallace's second of the season, after he previously notched a 12-yard grab in a Week 6 win over the Ravens. A key part of the Browns' special-teams coverage units, Wallace continues to handle a limited role on offense while the the team relies primarily on rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston and veteran Jerry Jeudy to fill out snaps at receiver.
injuryReports.injury: Wallace recorded a three-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.

injuryReports.name: Ryan Flournoy
injuryReports.returnComment: Flournoy had a chance to operate in a more prominent role on offense with George Pickens (hamstring) inactive, but Flournoy ultimately finished with his fewest catches since Week 3. The wide receiver helped set up Dallas for the game-winning score late in the fourth quarter, reeling in a deep ball from quarterback Dak Prescott for a 46-yard gain. Flournoy has now reeled in 32 of 47 targets for 395 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Flournoy caught two of three targets for 53 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Joey Porter Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jake Ferguson
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Donovan Ezeiruaku
injuryReports.returnComment: Ezeiruaku suffered an ankle injury in Sunday's meeting with the Colts and didn't return. While he hasn't been ruled out for Week 10 versus the 49ers, Ezeiruaku may not be able to suit up for that one. If that's the case, Von Miller and Marist Liufau could see more snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: George Pickens
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: P.J. Locke
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Brevyn Spann-Ford
injuryReports.returnComment: Spann-Ford opened Week 9 in his typical reserve role behind Jake Ferguson at tight end, but Ferguson suffered a knee injury in the third quarter. With Ferguson set to miss multiple weeks of action, Spann-Ford will have a chance to operate as the team's primary option at tight end beginning in Week 10 versus the 49ers. On the year, Spann-Ford has reeled in 19 of 27 targets for 136 yards and four touchdowns over nine regular-season contests so far.
injuryReports.injury: Spann-Ford caught two of three targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win versus the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Goodson
injuryReports.returnComment: Goodson likely will undergo further testing as the Cowboys look to hone in on a more definitive timeline for his return, but Schottenheimer's comments suggest that the reserve running back can safely be ruled out for at least Week 10 against the 49ers and Week 11 versus the Titans. Despite succumbing to the knee injury, the 25-year-old delivered his best performance of the season Sunday, finishing the day with 77 yards on 12 carries. The Cowboys currently have no other healthy running backs on the roster beyond starter Javonte Williams, but one or both of practice-squad members Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin will be candidates for elevation to the 53-man roster while Goodson is sidelined.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: KaVontae Turpin
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Ribs

injuryReports.name: DeMarvion Overshown
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Luke Schoonmaker
injuryReports.returnComment: out
injuryReports.injury: Groin

injuryReports.name: Brandon Aubrey
injuryReports.returnComment: Aubrey was able to convert multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game, but he did miss a kick for the second straight week. The kicker had makes from 45 and 28 yards in the contest, but he continued his long-range struggles Sunday, pulling a 50-yard attempt wide left late in the fourth quarter. Aubrey has now gone 17-for-22 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-8 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests to open the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Aubrey went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his PATs during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Dak Prescott
injuryReports.returnComment: Prescott had a couple of bumps in the road against an inconsistent Colts defense, but the veteran signal-caller, who was also working without George Pickens (hamstring), still found his way to his third 300-yard effort of the season. Prescott unsurprisingly bestowed plenty of attention on CeeDee Lamb, who ultimately was responsible for 10 of his completions, 195 of his yards and one of his two TDs. Prescott also connected with Jake Ferguson for a 10-yard scoring strike early in the second quarter, and the one blemish on the star quarterback's day was a  fumble on a sack at his own 16-yard line that led to a Colts touchdown. Prescott has at least one touchdown pass in every game heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Prescott completed 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for one yard in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Javonte Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams turned in one of his more efficient performances against an inconsistent Colts defense, ultimately managing his second 100-yard effort of the season. Williams continued to serve as a prolific supplier of touchdowns as well, recording his ninth rushing score of the campaign on a one-yard run with 1:08 remaining to seal the victory for Dallas. Williams' week-to-week yardage production has fluctuated a fair amount, but his high-volume role and trusted red-zone presence keeps him a must-play despite a tough Week 10 home matchup against the 49ers next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Williams rushed 20 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for 23 yards in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: CeeDee Lamb
injuryReports.returnComment: Lamb easily led the Cowboys across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets in a game that Dallas was operating without George Pickens (hamstring). Lamb's yardage total was a new season high, and he rounded out his stellar day with his seventh touchdown catch of the campaign on a 44-yard grab just before halftime. Even his turnover had a bright side to it from a fantasy perspective, as Lamb gained 44 yards on an impressive downfield catch and picked up extra yardage after the Colts initially failed to touch him down before fumbling at the end of that sequence. Lamb has four straight double-digit target games and is just 96 yards away from his sixth consecutive 1,000-yard season heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Lamb brought in 10 of 16 targets for 195 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Dee Winters
injuryReports.returnComment: Winters was evaluated for a concussion earlier in the second half but was ultimately cleared to return. That's a big boost to Dallas' defense, especially since fellow linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back) was unable to suit up Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Winters (head) has returned to Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Colts, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Jonathan Mingo
injuryReports.returnComment: Mingo was hurt in the second half and may not be able to return to the game. Prior to his exit, he caught one of three targets for 23 yards. With George Pickens (hamstring) and KaVontae Turpin (ribs) inactive Sunday, the Cowboys will be down to CeeDee Lamb, Ryan Flournoy, Camden Brown and Jordan Hudson at wideout if Mingo can't return.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Marist Liufau
injuryReports.returnComment: Liufau broke his left forearm in the Cowboys' preseason finale against the Saints and has yet to play in the 2026 regular season. The linebacker is set to make his debut in Sunday's contest after being activated from IR on Saturday.
injuryReports.injury: Liufau (forearm) is active for Sunday's game against the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Jonathan Bullard
